questions.question: Why does the guide recommend a "horizontal (platform-based)" rather than a "vertical (system-based)" approach to qualifying and auditing IT infrastructure?

options.A: The horizontal approach gives each application its own independent infrastructure, which reduces interaction between different systems
options.B: The vertical approach repeatedly deals with overlapping or even identical platform components, whereas the horizontal approach reduces overlap in documentation, qualification and audits
options.C: The horizontal approach requires every platform component to complete a full PQ one by one, so it lowers cost more than the vertical approach in the long run
options.D: The vertical approach is not applicable to any GxP system, so the guide requires platform components to be handled only by the horizontal approach

questions.explanation: The vertical (system-based) approach causes overlapping or identical platform components to be handled again and again, which is inefficient and impractical; the horizontal (platform-based) approach increases standardization and minimizes overlap in documentation, qualification and audits.

questions.question: In the context of IT infrastructure, how should the use of "validation" and "qualification" be distinguished?

options.A: Validation is used for platform components such as servers and networks, whereas qualification is used only for the GxP applications that run on them
options.B: The two are fully synonymous; both the platform and applications require full validation, with only the document naming differing
options.C: Qualification is limited to newly built platforms, while existing platforms already in operation are handled by validation with the same testing
options.D: Validation applies to the GxP applications running on the platform, while for the platform itself the focus should be on qualification of its components

questions.explanation: The guide reserves validation for GxP applications, while the platform focuses on component qualification. Some companies also use the term validation for critical infrastructure applications (such as password management and electronic signature verification), but the substantive compliance activities must still be consistent with the guide.

questions.topic: Adding an application to a qualified platform
questions.question: A company has already independently qualified its server and network platform and now wants to add a LIMS on top. Under the horizontal approach, what mainly needs to be done?

options.A: Only the LIMS application needs to be validated, and the qualified platform need not be redone; if the platform changes later, the risk to the GxP applications must still be assessed
options.B: A full IQ and OQ must be re-executed together with the whole platform, because adding any application changes the qualified state of the infrastructure, and this must be repeated every time any business application changes later
options.C: IT only needs to inform QA, because the platform is already qualified and adding an application requires no validation activity itself
options.D: The platform must first be split into infrastructure dedicated to that LIMS before qualification and audit can be carried out separately

questions.explanation: The platform and applications are qualified separately, so adding or changing a business application requires validating only that application. Conversely, changing an infrastructure component does not necessarily require revalidating the application, but the risk of each controlled change to GxP applications must still be assessed.

questions.question: According to Table 2.1, which description of the GAMP categories of "network building blocks" and "applications" is correct?

options.A: Network components are mostly HW category 3, while applications are SW category 1 or 2
options.B: Network components are mostly SW category 3 or 4, while applications are SW category 1 or 2
options.C: Network building blocks are mostly HW category 1 and SW category 1 or 2, while applications are SW category 3, 4 or 5
options.D: Network building blocks are mostly HW category 1, and applications are the same as the network, SW category 1 or 2

questions.explanation: Most network building blocks are HW category 1 and SW category 1 or 2 (custom cables being the exception, at HW category 2); applications are SW category 3, 4 or 5, and their validation is outside the scope of this guide.

questions.question: Which of the following is explicitly included in the scope of this guide?

options.A: Overall Business Continuity Planning led by business users
options.B: Alternative operating procedures needed by business processes when infrastructure fails
options.C: Validation methodology for GxP applications built on the platform
options.D: Disaster recovery and contingency planning for the IT infrastructure itself

questions.explanation: The guide considers disaster recovery and contingency planning for the IT infrastructure. However, Business Continuity Planning should be led by business users and system/data owners and is out of scope; alternative operating procedures during failures and application validation are also outside the scope.

questions.question: According to Section 3.5, when an entry in a qualification test record is wrong, which correction method meets the requirements?

options.A: Cover the original entry with correction fluid and note in the test report summary that corrections were made, with no signature or date by the executing person needed as long as the page looks tidy
options.B: Fill in the whole test form again and destroy the original form, to keep the test records tidy and consistent
options.C: Do not obscure the original entry, and clearly record the date, reason and person making the correction, or use a computerized tool that generates an audit trail automatically
options.D: QA corrects everything uniformly at review, and test executors must not change anything already entered on the spot

questions.explanation: A correction must not cover the original entry and must clearly show the date, the reason and the identity of the person making it, or use a computerized tool with an automatic audit trail. Records should also reflect actual observed results, not just pass/fail.

questions.question: Comparing Section 3.8 Periodic Review with Section 3.9 QA audit, which statement is correct?

options.A: A Periodic Review can be performed by an SME or IT Quality and Compliance, with scope and frequency determined by risk; an audit must be performed by QA personnel independent of the audited unit
options.B: A Periodic Review must be performed by independent QA, while an audit may be done by SMEs of the audited unit themselves to grasp all details, and conclusions of neither need QA review or approval to take effect
options.C: Both are fixed at once a year, with scope decided by the head of the unit reviewed, without considering risk or past problem history
options.D: A Periodic Review is performed only after major upgrades, in an event-driven manner, while an audit is performed only once per cycle on a fixed schedule

questions.explanation: A Periodic Review is performed by an SME or IT Quality and Compliance, with scope, depth and frequency determined by impact and risk, and can also be event-driven; an audit must be performed by QA personnel independent of the audited group, with scope, frequency and purpose decided by QA.

questions.question: A legacy platform has run stably for years but has never been formally qualified, and intensive testing could affect its continued operation. What does the guide recommend as the basis for further planning?

options.A: Reinstall all running components immediately to collect complete IQ documentation as a basis for filling gaps
options.B: Prepare an "Experience Report" that compiles the platform's inventory, operating status and history as the basis for further planning
options.C: Run comprehensive stress and load testing on the whole platform first, to confirm it can keep operating under extreme conditions
options.D: Decommission it and replace it with a new platform, since an old platform that has not been qualified cannot meet GxP requirements

questions.explanation: For a legacy platform that operates stably, intensive testing may itself affect operation, so an Experience Report is recommended first. Reinstalling properly working components just to obtain IQ documents is not necessarily appropriate, and stress/load testing is not a priority for stably operating platforms.

questions.question: The platform management group is unsure which infrastructure components need qualification and how important each component is. According to Section 4.1, how should this be handled?

options.A: Infrastructure staff independently judge the GxP impact of each component, since they know the technical details of the platform best, without input from application or data owners and without QA involvement
options.B: Do not qualify for now, and carry out risk assessment and related testing only after an inspector points out deficiencies
options.C: Assess only the components used by GxP applications; non-GxP applications operating on the same infrastructure need no special consideration
options.D: The application/data owners and QA define it; if no criticality is specified, the platform group may apply the same high standard to all components and data

questions.explanation: The application/data owners and QA define which components need qualification; infrastructure staff should not be expected to assess GxP compliance independently. Non-GxP applications on the same infrastructure may also affect GxP applications and must be identified and controlled in the risk assessment.

questions.question: Regarding the two qualification strategy scenarios in Section 5.1, which statement is correct?

options.A: When platform requirements are derived case by case from application system specifications, the building block concept is hard to exploit fully, close interaction with system owners is needed, and qualification is mostly one-off
options.B: When platform requirements are derived case by case from application system specifications, the qualified platform is treated as a commodity, qualification plans are mostly written in SOPs, and there is little interaction with owners
options.C: When the platform specification is independent of applications, every platform must be tailor-designed for a specific application one by one, and qualification is also mostly a one-off effort
options.D: When the platform specification is independent of applications, requirements are mainly derived from application system specifications, and close interaction with system owners is needed before qualification can begin

questions.explanation: Scenario 1 (specification independent of applications) suits the building block approach, with plans usually written in SOPs, little interaction with system owners, and the platform treated as a commodity; Scenario 2 (requirements derived case by case from application specifications) involves much interaction, and platform qualification is mostly one-off.

questions.question: Why does Section 5.6.2.3 recommend preparing and maintaining a "Configuration Items List (CIL)" for servers?

options.A: To replace the role of the IQ, since once the CIL is approved the actual installed parameters and versions of the server need no further verification
options.B: For users to record daily operations and login records, and as the only source of evidence in a Periodic Review
options.C: Only for price comparison and acceptance at the procurement stage, with no real effect on later server replication, rebuilding or IQ verification
options.D: To allow the verified configuration to be safely rebuilt or replicated into identical servers, and to serve as the basis for verifying versions and settings during IQ

questions.explanation: The CIL records hardware (make and model, memory, CPU and number of disks, etc.) and software (operating system, service packs, patches, access and network settings, etc.) items, identified by version number, so that servers can be safely rebuilt or replicated and verified against it during IQ.

questions.question: In a global IT infrastructure, according to Section 5.4.2.3, to what should system time synchronization be traceable at a minimum?

options.A: The local time of each region's time zone, with each site managing its own daylight saving and standard time offsets
options.B: The factory-set values of the built-in clock of each server, adjusted by users themselves when they find errors
options.C: An international standard (such as UTC or TAI), or at least the company's time standard
options.D: A time source designated by the application supplier, with no need to cross-check against the time of other systems

questions.explanation: The guide requires time synchronization to be traceable to an international standard (such as UTC or TAI), at a minimum to the company time standard; the time management specification must be verified in IQ and OQ, and the responsibility and access rights for setting or resetting system time must be documented.

questions.question: Regarding storage systems, which statement correctly distinguishes SAN from NAS?

options.A: A SAN is a single server plus disk array attached to the ordinary network; a NAS has its own dedicated high-speed network and dedicated network components
options.B: A SAN has its own high-speed network and dedicated network components; a NAS is not attached to a separate network but is a dedicated server plus disk array
options.C: IQ and OQ for both can be done directly on the storage device itself, with no need to go through any connected server
options.D: The design of both SAN and NAS is independent of expected load and network topology, and standard models recommended by the supplier are simply selected

questions.explanation: A SAN has its own high-speed network (routers, hubs, switches, gateways); a NAS is not attached to a separate network and is a dedicated server plus disk array. Design depends on the expected load and network topology, and in practice OQ can only be done through a connected server.

questions.question: A client machine has a GxP application installed, and management requires that any modification other than high-priority security patches go through formal change management and complete qualification of the change. Which category should it be classified in?

options.A: 'Controlled': all modifications other than high-priority security patches require formal change management and qualification of the change
options.B: 'Restricted': users cannot modify it but it still accepts centrally controlled updates, and changes need no separate qualification, so no software change on this client needs any review or testing
options.C: 'Un-restricted': users may modify it, as long as it complies with company security and general software policy and accepts central updates
options.D: 'Thin': accessed through a web interface, with all data and software on the server side, so the client needs no change management

questions.explanation: The guide's typical classification is un-restricted, restricted and controlled; for controlled, all modifications (except possibly high-priority security patches) must go through formal change management and qualification of the change. A client hosting a GxP application should be managed more strictly than one used only for email.

questions.question: The evaluation committee reviews a supplier's delivery record and collected information and finds them not fully satisfactory but not yet unacceptable. According to Section 5.6.1, what is the most appropriate classification and treatment?

options.A: Approved: because the supplier has a delivery record, it can be put straight on the approved list and exempted from additional testing and witnessing
options.B: Not approved: as soon as the information is not fully satisfactory, all purchasing and dealings must stop immediately and no more deliveries accepted, all existing customers must be notified, and existing contracts and all open orders terminated
options.C: Conditionally approved: risk can be reduced through closer follow-up and more intensive testing and witnessing than originally planned
options.D: Leave unclassified: wait until a second audit is completed to decide whether to purchase, with all delivered items returned to the supplier in the meantime

questions.explanation: When information or delivery records are not fully satisfactory, the supplier is Conditionally approved, and risk can be mitigated through closer follow-up and more intensive testing/witnessing; Not approved applies when information or records are insufficient or unsatisfactory. Items for improvement after a first audit are not necessarily a problem.

questions.topic: Focus of OQ for standard platforms
questions.question: If the platform consists entirely of commercially available standard products, where does Section 5.7 recommend the OQ focus?

options.A: Testing connectivity, and capacity where applicable, using built-in or add-on computerized tools, rather than testing core functionality
options.B: Full functional testing of each standard product's core functions, replacing the supplier's own factory tests and requiring the company to repeat all factory tests and certification procedures the supplier has already completed
options.C: Only reviewing certificates and manuals issued by the supplier, with the company itself doing no operational testing or verification
options.D: Stress testing with a large number of simultaneous user logins, as an OQ item that must be performed for every standard platform

questions.explanation: For commercially available standard products, OQ focuses on connectivity (and capacity where applicable) rather than core functionality. OQ should have at least a set of instructions describing the test steps, expected results and evidence to be collected, designed according to the outcome of the earlier risk assessment.

questions.topic: Firewall OQ - positive and negative testing
questions.question: When OQ verifies the critical functions of a firewall, what testing approach does Section 5.7 recommend?

options.A: Test only that traffic that should be allowed passes, because blocked traffic is confirmed by the supplier
options.B: Test both positively and negatively: traffic that should pass does pass, and traffic that should be blocked is indeed blocked
options.C: Only check that the firewall rule list matches the design documents, without actually sending any network packets
options.D: Test the firewall only at the application PQ stage; infrastructure OQ does not address firewall functions

questions.explanation: The guide requires firewall OQ to include positive and negative testing, i.e. allowing traffic that should pass and blocking traffic that should be blocked. Other typical tests in the same section include confirming that default passwords have been changed and time synchronization.

questions.question: According to Section 6.2, at what level are Configuration Items (CIs) usually defined?

options.A: At the level of a whole machine room or entire platform, without splitting into individual components to avoid excessive management burden, and prohibiting anyone from creating separate version or change records for individual components
options.B: Hardware and software only, excluding critical parameter settings and documentation, since the latter two are handled separately by change management
options.C: At the level of each application, with the application owner deciding whether to include it within infrastructure management
options.D: Defined at the lowest level at which a component can be independently installed, replaced or modified, covering hardware, software, critical parameters and documentation

questions.explanation: A CI includes hardware, software, critical parameter settings, documentation and any part of the infrastructure the company wants to control, usually defined at the lowest level at which it can be independently installed, replaced or modified. At least the items critical to maintaining the qualified state should be placed under CM to provide an approved baseline.

questions.question: According to Section 6.7 Problem Management, what is the difference between a "problem" and a "known error"?

options.A: A problem is a failure for which a temporary workaround has been found; a known error is an event whose root cause is not yet known
options.B: A problem is every call a user logs with the Help Desk; a known error is one of those calls that has been closed, and no problem may be logged by the Help Desk, only created directly by management
options.C: A problem is the unknown underlying cause of one or more incidents; a known error is a problem that has been successfully diagnosed and for which a workaround exists
options.D: A problem refers to a hardware failure and a known error to a software failure, and both must be handled through the change management group

questions.explanation: A problem is the unknown root cause of one or more incidents; a problem that has been successfully diagnosed and has a workaround is called a known error. All logged problems must be tracked and resolved through an approved channel, and those needing a change are handed to the Change Management Group.

questions.question: When an old platform is retired and data must be migrated to a new platform, which of the following does the guide require to be assured in writing?

options.A: Every record on the old platform must be compared manually one by one, with no statistical methods or computerized tools allowed, and all data on the old platform must be destroyed immediately after migration with no backup kept
options.B: All data elements have been migrated, important data attributes (such as security settings) are retained, and no unintended extra data elements are present
options.C: The new platform may have more records than the old one, as long as the records added after migration are verbally confirmed by users afterwards
options.D: Only confirmation that the main business data have migrated is needed; supporting data and the results of data conversion are outside the scope of written assurance

questions.explanation: The guide lists what needs written assurance: all data elements migrated, critical attributes retained, supporting data correctly transferred, no unexpected extra data elements, and consistent results for specified conversions. The verification method depends on risk and can use statistical methods or automated tools; it does not necessarily require manual comparison of every record.

questions.question: A company leases IT infrastructure services from a service provider. According to Appendix 1, which statement is correct?

options.A: Because the facility is owned by the supplier, responsibility for qualification status transfers to the supplier under the contract, and the company only pays on time
options.B: The company can reduce its own Control and Compliance burden simply by outsourcing the ownership and quality assurance of systems and data
options.C: The company remains responsible for the qualification status and must set expectations and monitor continuously, for example by negotiating, agreeing, funding and monitoring the SLA
options.D: The company need only audit the supplier once at signing, after which the supplier itself ensures the SLA is met and the company need not follow up

questions.explanation: Whether infrastructure is owned or leased, the regulated company is responsible for the qualification status and must set out expectations and monitor continuously. Ownership and QA of systems and data should not be outsourced, for Control and Compliance reasons.

questions.topic: When to appoint a Data Owner
questions.question: A file storage service hosts data for many users, and the data are not logically owned by an application owner. According to Appendix 1, what is the more appropriate practice?

options.A: The platform administrator becomes the owner of all data directly, with users only entering data and bearing no responsibility, and alone decides retention and deletion of all data with no one's approval
options.B: Appoint no owner, since the data merely reside on the server and quality and security are left entirely to the supplier
options.C: Independent QA acts as data owner and is responsible for the day-to-day actual work of backup, restore and archiving
options.D: Appoint a data owner, who ensures that quality and security measures are adequate, for example backup and restore, archiving, audit trail, access restriction and availability

questions.explanation: When the data stored in a system are not logically owned by an application owner, the company may appoint a data owner; they must ensure that the quality and security measures put in place are adequate, and be informed of their responsibilities and have the means to fulfil them.

questions.topic: Independent QA vs IT Quality and Compliance
questions.question: Comparing Independent QA with IT Quality and Compliance, which statement is consistent with Appendix 1?

options.A: Independent QA bears ultimate responsibility for achieving and maintaining compliance; IT Quality and Compliance escalates matters such as critical documents to QA for approval
options.B: IT Quality and Compliance is independent of QA and has final approval authority over critical changes and decisions on record retention periods
options.C: The two roles are in fact the same, so there is no need to document separately the relationship between them and the delegation of activities, and QA need not approve any document, retention period or major change at all
options.D: Independent QA is responsible for daily platform operation and technical support; IT Quality and Compliance is responsible for final audit conclusions

questions.explanation: QA, independent of IT, bears ultimate responsibility for achieving and maintaining compliance; IT Quality and Compliance provides professional support and escalates matters such as approval of critical documents, technical record retention periods and critical changes to QA for approval. The relationship and delegation between them should be documented.

questions.question: The GAMP risk assessment in Appendix 2 has two stages. What are the outputs of each stage?

options.A: Stage 1 produces the risk priority; Stage 2 then classifies each hazard into one of three levels
options.B: Stage 1 classifies each hazard into one of three levels; Stage 2 brings in mitigating factors such as probability of detection to arrive at the risk priority
options.C: Both stages output only a single high/medium/low score, with no need to consider probability of detection or other mitigating factors
options.D: Stage 1 decides the number of test cases; Stage 2 decides which platform owner approves the final report

questions.explanation: Stage 1 classifies each hazard into one of three levels based on factors such as impact and likelihood of occurrence; Stage 2 then evaluates mitigating factors (such as the probability of detection before the hazard occurs), with the output being the risk priority. A risk evaluation then follows to judge whether the risk is acceptable, documenting results and assumptions.

questions.question: According to the explanation of type and instance in Appendix 3, which statement is correct?

options.A: Instance qualification includes all deliverable documents, whereas type qualification includes only instance IQ and OQ
options.B: Type and instance are only different names, and both require the PO, SME and QA to review all documents together
options.C: Every instance must have complete requirements and design specifications written afresh, and may not reference building block documents
options.D: Type qualification covers everything except instance IQ and OQ; an instance includes only instance IQ and OQ and references the type documents

questions.explanation: A type is the generic specification and derived documents of a building block (standard configuration), and its qualification covers everything other than instance IQ and OQ; instance qualification consists only of instance IQ and OQ and references the type documents. In Table A3.1, the SME is responsible for instance IQ/OQ.

questions.topic: Authorization to restore in SOP table
questions.question: According to Table A4.1, under which category of SOP does the "Restore process (including authorization to restore)" fall?

options.A: Logical security under Security, regulated together with account and password management
options.B: Data backup and restore under Data management, alongside backup scheduling and media management
options.C: Disaster recovery under Continuity management, regulated together with the business continuity plan
options.D: Client installation under Client management, together with the evolution of the standard client

questions.explanation: Table A4.1 lists backup scheduling, logging, verification, media labeling and storage, risk analysis, and the restore process including authorization to restore all under data backup and restore in Data management. To restore data, it must be confirmed that the requester is authorized to restore and also to view that data.

questions.question: In Table A4.1, what are the typical deliverables of "Continuity management (disaster recovery and contingency planning)"?

options.A: The Disaster Recovery Plan (part of the business continuity plan) and Disaster Recovery Test Reports
options.B: Backup logs, restore logs and data deletion logs, as the main evidence of daily operation and data management
options.C: Organization charts, job descriptions and training records, to show that relevant personnel are qualified to carry out disaster recovery
options.D: Access control logs and password update logs, to show that unauthorized access attempts were detected and dealt with

questions.explanation: The typical deliverables of continuity management are the Disaster Recovery Plan (as part of business continuity planning) and Disaster Recovery Test Reports. The other options belong to documents of the data management, general management (personnel) or security categories respectively.

questions.question: Table A5.1 says there should be a procedure to ensure that setting the system time does not disturb the sequence of any log entries. What is the example practice?

options.A: Adjust the time forward or backward in one step to the correct value, with a handwritten note in the log of the reason for the adjustment
options.B: Adjust only at the annual switch between daylight saving and standard time, otherwise leaving each system's clock to run on its own
options.C: Always adjust forward, in small, frequent increments, to avoid disrupting the log sequence
options.D: Adjusting backward is permitted at any time, as long as QA checks the logs afterwards during the Periodic Review

questions.explanation: The example practice is to adjust ahead, in small and frequent increments, to avoid time going backward or jumping greatly and breaking the log sequence. The same checklist also asks whether there is a dedicated time server traceable to a reliable source such as BIPM, and whether the effect of daylight saving/standard time settings on timestamps has been assessed.

questions.question: According to Appendix 5, how should a company use the Periodic Review checklist in Table A5.1?

options.A: Every Periodic Review must work through every question in full, and omitting any question means the review is incomplete
options.B: Use it only for GxP elements; non-GxP infrastructure elements must never be included in the scope of a Periodic Review
options.C: The reviewed unit decides on the day of the review which questions to answer, without agreeing in advance with the people concerned
options.D: Consider possible hazards and risks beforehand, define and agree the topics to be covered, and then select the applicable ones from the list as appropriate

questions.explanation: Appendix 5 states that a company should define and agree in advance the topics to be covered in each Periodic Review, taking hazards and risks into account; the full list is not always needed or applicable and can be selected from as appropriate. A company may also include non-GxP elements in the review for business reasons.

questions.question: External contract staff need temporary network access. How does the Table A5.1 checklist expect such accounts to be handled?

options.A: Set an expiry date, and subject them, like permanent employees, to removal procedures on leaving or transfer and to Periodic Review of dormant accounts
options.B: Share the same account and password with permanent employees, so as not to add to the burden of user lists and account management, with accounts valid permanently whether or not the person has left and never reviewed to see if still in use
options.C: Set no expiry date, and after the contract ends the department head remembers to notify IT, which then deactivates the account manually
options.D: Create no logical account, only issuing a physical access card, so that they log in with another person's account to complete system work

questions.explanation: The checklist asks whether the procedure covers both permanent and temporary/contract staff, whether temporary accounts have an expiry date, whether they are removed when staff leave or transfer, and whether obsolete or dormant accounts are reviewed regularly. Logical access should also consist of at least two elements, with the combination unique to each person.

questions.question: A security vulnerability has been confirmed by the supplier and user groups and poses an immediate and real threat to the company's business. According to Appendix 6, in which category should the patch be classified?

options.A: Update: no immediate threat; consider handling it together in the next scheduled platform upgrade
options.B: Urgent Update: a threat is likely, and the patching must be done within a specified time frame
options.C: Routine Change: no change control needed, but all relevant system owners should be informed afterwards
options.D: Emergency Fix: the threat is immediate and real, and it should be applied as soon as possible, with change documentation completed afterwards

questions.explanation: The guide divides security update urgency into three categories: Emergency Fix (immediate and real threat, applied as soon as possible), Urgent Update (likely threat, applied within a specified time) and Update (no immediate threat, included in the next scheduled upgrade). Change control for an emergency change may be completed afterwards, but must be done in the shortest possible time.

questions.topic: Level of testing after a platform upgrade
questions.question: The platform hosting a GxP system is to be upgraded; the technical assessment considers it a major change that is likely to affect the application and is not an emergency change. According to Appendix 7, which level of testing should be used?

options.A: No Testing: because a platform upgrade is within the infrastructure domain, no testing of the applications above is needed
options.B: Confirmation Testing: only minimal documented testing to confirm that the application runs on the updated platform
options.C: Full Testing: full regression testing of the application on the updated platform
options.D: Confidence Testing: testing only a representative subset of functions against predefined specifications

questions.explanation: When an update is major and likely to affect the application, especially a business-critical or GxP system, full (regression) testing should be performed. A minor update may need only confirmation testing; for highly critical systems or significant updates, confidence testing should at least be considered.

questions.question: According to Appendix 6 Section 2.3, which pairing of the three types of security control is correct?

options.A: Administrative controls: security awareness training and incident management; technical controls: access control mechanisms and password management; physical controls: controlling people's access to facilities and perimeter protection
options.B: Administrative controls: password management and authentication methods; technical controls: policies, standards and procedures; physical controls: arrangements for security awareness training and incident management
options.C: Administrative controls: controlling people's access to facilities and perimeter protection; technical controls: security awareness training and incident management; physical controls: access control mechanisms and resource management
options.D: Administrative controls: perimeter protection and intrusion monitoring; technical controls: access control to control people entering facilities; physical controls: development of policies, standards, procedures and guidelines

questions.explanation: Administrative controls include policies, standards, procedures, guidelines, security awareness training and incident management; technical controls include access control mechanisms, password and resource management, identification and authentication, and security devices; physical controls include controlling people's access to facilities, locks, perimeter protection and intrusion monitoring, and removal of unnecessary optical drives.

questions.topic: Audit findings at an outsourcing provider
questions.question: Nonconformities are found when auditing an outsourcing service provider. According to Appendix 8, which statement is correct?

options.A: The supplier decides for itself whether to correct, and the regulated company need only record the results in an annual report
options.B: The regulated company is responsible for authorizing appropriate resolution or mitigation, and tracks it to closure in its own CAPA program
options.C: Audit findings are an internal matter of the supplier, and the regulated company's QA may not repeat the same audit afterwards
options.D: The supplier need not give a written response; agreeing to improve in verbal discussion is regarded as correction already complete

questions.explanation: The regulated company must authorize appropriate resolution or mitigation and track it to closure in the CAPA program to show control; the supplier should provide a formal written response and, as needed, draw up and carry out an improvement plan. The company's QA should also be allowed to repeat audits at appropriate intervals or in specific circumstances.

questions.question: What is the minimum requirement for backup recommended in Appendix 9?

options.A: A full backup every day, with no incremental or differential backups and no retention of any historical backups
options.B: A full backup once a month and no backup at other times, with users keeping copies of important files themselves
options.C: A full backup on one day each week and incremental or differential backups on the other days, with historical backups retained as needed
options.D: Daily incremental backups, with a full backup made only once when the system goes live and once when retired, and no backups in between

questions.explanation: The recommended minimum is a full backup one day a week and incremental or differential backups on the other days, with historical backups kept as appropriate. Backups should be monitored, including reviewing backup logs, periodically confirming that all required systems are included in the schedule, and managing backup media.

questions.question: According to Appendix 10, how is compatibility of client security patches recommended to be verified before full rollout?

options.A: Tested in a test laboratory with representative software and hardware, and with a pilot installation in the real environment without impact, included in the qualification plan
options.B: The supplier guarantees compatibility and the company needs no separate testing, to avoid delaying the introduction of security patches, and owners of business-critical applications are never informed, with IT deciding alone
options.C: Installed on all clients in the company at once, with machines rolled back one by one after problems appear, to achieve coverage as fast as possible
options.D: Users decide for themselves whether to install, with the client management group only collecting users' feedback afterwards

questions.explanation: Patches must be tested for compatibility with the operating system, office software and client software; there should be a test laboratory and pilot installation so that problems are found before full rollout. The supplier's patch information should also be given to owners of business-critical applications so that they can test before rollout.

questions.topic: Thick vs thin client and user modifications
questions.question: Regarding Appendix 10's explanation of user modifications on clients, which statement is correct?

options.A: A PC running a thin client carries higher risk, so for GxP applications a thin client must always be set to controlled
options.B: Whether thick or thin, all clients should be open to modification by users themselves, to maintain user productivity
options.C: The risk of modifying a group of clients is the same as modifying a single client, so there is no need to manage it separately under an SOP
options.D: A PC running a thick client often needs to be restricted or even controlled for GxP applications; a thin client (such as web-based) is less likely to cause data modification or availability problems

questions.explanation: Many GxP applications require PCs running a thick client to be restricted or even controlled to ensure data are not lost or modified without authorization; thin clients (such as web-based technology) are less likely to cause data modification or availability problems. Modifying a group of clients carries more risk than modifying a single client, and all modifications should be managed under an SOP.

questions.question: According to Appendix 11 Section 6.1, what are the two main elements of an SNMP network management system?

options.A: Server and Client: the Server stores device data, and the Client displays reports to users
options.B: Manager and Agents: the Manager is the console operated by the administrator, and the Agents interface with the managed devices
options.C: Collector and Probe: the Collector gathers event messages, and the Probe converts messages into reports
options.D: Router and Switch: the Router manages network configuration, and the Switch reports device performance data

questions.explanation: The two main elements of SNMP are the Manager and Agents. The Manager is the network administrator's console, often paired with a data management system that stores configuration, alerts (traps) and performance history; Agents interface with the managed devices (bridges, hubs, routers, servers, etc.). SNMP is the de facto standard because of its simplicity.

questions.question: In the network performance example of Table A11.1, what are the alert limit and action limit for "Collision rate (percent of network time)"?

options.A: Alert limit > 10%, action limit > 20%
options.B: Alert limit > 0.5%, action limit > 5%
options.C: Alert limit > 0.1%, action limit > 1.0%
options.D: Alert limit > 2%, action limit > 5%

questions.explanation: The collision rate example is alert > 0.1% and action > 1.0%. Alert > 10% / action > 20% is the example for 24-hour average load, and alert > 2% / action > 5% is the example for BCast/MCast. These quantitative values come from actual cases and serve only as a reference for companies setting their own metrics and limits; they are not mandated absolute values.

questions.question: According to the Appendix 12 Glossary, what is the difference between an "assessment" and an "audit"?

options.A: Both must be performed by persons independent of the party being evaluated; an assessment merely has fewer documentation requirements than an audit
options.B: An assessment is performed by an SME or IT Quality and Compliance and need not be independent; an audit is a systematic, independent and documented process
options.C: An assessment must be performed by an external organization, whereas an audit is limited to company staff and needs no documented records
options.D: The two have the same definition, except that an assessment is used for hardware platforms and an audit for review of software applications

questions.explanation: An assessment is an investigation of a process, system or platform by an SME or IT Quality and Compliance and need not be independent; an audit (ISO/GAMP) is a systematic, independent and documented process of objectively evaluating evidence to determine the extent to which agreed criteria are fulfilled.
